presentation.title: One-Time Passcode Account Takeover
presentation.summary: Practice responding when a bank-looking alert and caller use genuine security messages to try to reset access, enroll a device, and move money.
presentation.practiceGoal: Keep one-time codes private, deny sign-ins you did not start, and secure sessions, devices, profile details, and payees through the real bank.

warningSigns.sign: An unexpected text and incoming caller claimed that a transfer had to be canceled immediately.
The caller used partial personal or card information as proof of identity.
A genuine security message said never to share the one-time code, while the caller asked for that code.
A sign-in or device-enrollment prompt appeared even though the learner did not start one.
Contact details, devices, payees, or transfers changed while the caller discouraged independent bank contact.

finalReview.safestAction: Leave the incoming text or call, open a known bank app or use a trusted bank number, and deny any code, sign-in, or device approval you did not initiate.

realWorldActions.action: A real bank security code or device prompt can be triggered by a scammer. The genuine message does not make the caller genuine.
Never read a one-time passcode to an unexpected caller or enter it on a page that caller supplied.
If access may have changed, ask the real bank to review active sessions, enrolled devices, contact information, payees, and recent transactions.
Secure the email and phone accounts connected to banking, not only the bank password.
If money moved, report it promptly and preserve records. Recovery is not guaranteed.

artifact.senderStatus: Displayed name only; sender not independently verified
artifact.heading: Did you authorize a $2,400 transfer?
artifact.message: A simulated text says a $2,400 transfer is pending and provides a link. Seconds later, caller ID displays the fictional bank's name.
artifact.transcript: A bank-looking simulated text says, "Did you authorize a $2,400 transfer? Act now to cancel." It supplies a link. Seconds later, an incoming call displays the name of fictional Riverbend Community Bank. The text, link, and caller ID have not been independently verified. No real account or transfer is involved.

scene.question: How should you verify the alert?
scene.description: The incoming channels may be connected to each other without being connected to the real bank.

warningSigns.sign: The alert and call are unexpected.
The message supplies its own link.
The amount and urgency are designed to prompt a quick response.

choice.title: Use the known bank app or a trusted number
choice.subtitle: Do not use the link or incoming call.

feedback.heading: You selected an independent channel
feedback.consequence: The real account shows no matching transfer.
feedback.explanation: A known app or trusted number is not controlled by the incoming contact.

warningSigns.sign: The alert supplied the path it wanted you to use.

choice.title: Answer the call but share nothing
choice.subtitle: Listen to the supposed fraud representative.

feedback.heading: The caller keeps an opportunity to persuade
feedback.consequence: The caller uses partial personal information to sound legitimate.
feedback.explanation: Refusing information is protective, but caller ID and a convincing story still do not verify the caller.

warningSigns.sign: The caller reached you through the unverified alert.

choice.title: Reply to the text or open its link
choice.subtitle: Use the incoming message before checking the real account.

feedback.heading: The unverified contact gains engagement
feedback.consequence: A simulated caller-supplied page and follow-up call continue the cancellation story.
feedback.explanation: Replying can confirm engagement, and a supplied page can support the same impersonation. No credential form is used in this simulation.

warningSigns.sign: The sender chose both the claim and the response route.

artifact.callerStatus: Fictional identity; incoming caller not verified
artifact.heading: The caller already knows a few details
artifact.message: Jamie states the learner's name, home city, and the last four digits of a card, then asks for date of birth or Social Security number digits to confirm identity.
artifact.transcript: The simulated caller uses the fictional name Jamie Cole and claims to represent Riverbend Community Bank. Jamie states the learner's name, home city, and the last four digits of a card, then asks for more sensitive information. Stolen, purchased, or publicly available details can make an impersonator sound informed.

scene.question: Does the caller's knowledge prove legitimacy?
scene.description: Information a caller knows is not the same as an identity check you control.

warningSigns.sign: The call was not initiated through a trusted bank channel.
The caller uses known details to request more sensitive details.
The supposed cancellation remains urgent.

choice.title: Refuse and call the bank independently
choice.subtitle: End the incoming call before confirming anything.

feedback.heading: You did not let known details verify the caller
feedback.consequence: The real bank confirms that the caller was not handling a legitimate transfer.
feedback.explanation: Partial information can be exposed without giving a caller authority.

warningSigns.sign: The caller wanted more information than the learner had requested help with.

choice.title: Confirm only the home city
choice.subtitle: Keep more sensitive information private.

feedback.heading: A limited detail is confirmed
feedback.consequence: The caller continues and triggers a real one-time-code message.
feedback.explanation: The most sensitive information remains private, but the unverified caller still controls the conversation.

warningSigns.sign: The caller uses each answer to build momentum.

choice.title: Provide sensitive identity or account details
choice.subtitle: Help Jamie confirm the account.

feedback.heading: Sensitive information is exposed
feedback.consequence: The caller has more material for account recovery or identity theft and triggers a security code.
feedback.explanation: A bank should not need an unexpected caller to collect information this way.

warningSigns.sign: The caller requested date-of-birth, Social Security, card, or username information.

artifact.heading: Transfer cancellation review
artifact.message: The caller-supplied page repeats the $2,400 claim while Jamie calls and recites partial personal information as proof.
artifact.transcript: The simulated page at a fictional dot-example domain repeats the pending-transfer story but contains no functional sign-in or credential form. During a follow-up call, Jamie states the learner's name, city, and partial card information, then asks for more sensitive details. A polished page and known information can both be part of the same scam.

scene.question: How should you respond to the page and caller?
scene.description: The page and caller confirm each other because the same operation controls both.

warningSigns.sign: The page came from the unverified text.
The caller knows details that may have been exposed elsewhere.
The page sends the learner back to the caller.

choice.title: Close the page and contact the bank independently
choice.subtitle: Use the saved app or a trusted number.

feedback.heading: You left the caller-controlled channels
feedback.consequence: The real bank disproves the pending-transfer claim.
feedback.explanation: The page and caller cannot independently verify each other.

warningSigns.sign: Both channels originated with the same unexpected message.

choice.title: Confirm only the city
choice.subtitle: Keep sensitive details private but remain on the call.

feedback.heading: The caller continues with limited confirmation
feedback.consequence: Jamie triggers a real security-code message.
feedback.explanation: Even a small confirmation can keep the manipulation moving.

warningSigns.sign: The caller still has not been independently verified.

choice.title: Provide sensitive details to the page or caller
choice.subtitle: Try to complete the cancellation review.

feedback.heading: The exposure deepens
feedback.consequence: The scammer gains identity or account-recovery information and triggers a security code.
feedback.explanation: A caller-supplied page is not a safe place to verify an unexpected contact.

warningSigns.sign: Sensitive information is requested before independent bank contact.

artifact.senderStatus: Genuine simulated bank-security message; triggered by an unknown attempt
artifact.heading: Your verification code is 482193
artifact.message: Bank employees will never ask for this code. Do not share it. The code is fictional and cannot authorize a real action.
artifact.transcript: A genuine simulated security text from the fictional bank reads, "Your verification code is 482193. Bank employees will never ask for this code. Do not share it." Jamie says the code will cancel the transfer. The message can be genuine because the scammer triggered a real password-reset or device-enrollment attempt. A genuine code does not make the caller genuine.

scene.question: What should you do with the code?
scene.description: The warning inside the real message is more reliable than the unexpected caller's explanation.

warningSigns.sign: The caller asks for a code that says not to share it.
The learner did not request the code.
The caller calls an authorization code a cancellation code.

choice.title: Read the warning, refuse, and end the call
choice.subtitle: Contact the bank independently.

feedback.heading: You protected the authorization code
feedback.consequence: The caller cannot complete the attempted reset with this code.
feedback.explanation: A one-time code authorizes access or an action. It is not a cancellation tool for an unexpected caller.

warningSigns.sign: The real message directly contradicted the caller.

choice.title: Ask why the message says not to share it
choice.subtitle: Challenge Jamie while staying on the call.

feedback.heading: The caller explains away the warning
feedback.consequence: Jamie says the warning is generic and triggers a new-device approval request.
feedback.explanation: Questioning the request is useful, but the safest response is to end the call. The caller can trigger another genuine prompt.

warningSigns.sign: The caller treats a clear safety warning as an exception.

choice.title: Read the code aloud
choice.subtitle: Let Jamie cancel the supposed transfer.

feedback.heading: The code authorizes the attacker's attempt
feedback.consequence: The scammer advances a password reset or device enrollment.
feedback.explanation: The code belongs only in an action the learner personally started.

warningSigns.sign: The caller requested a code the message said to keep private.

artifact.senderStatus: Genuine simulated bank-security message; sensitive details may already be exposed
artifact.heading: Your verification code is 482193
artifact.message: Bank employees will never ask for this code. Do not share it. The code is fictional and nonfunctional.
artifact.transcript: A genuine simulated message from fictional Riverbend Community Bank contains code 482193 and says bank employees will never ask for it. Jamie asks the learner to share it to cancel the transfer. Because sensitive information may already have been disclosed, refusing the code stops one step but a broader account review is still appropriate.

scene.question: What should you do after earlier information exposure?
scene.description: Do not share the code, and address the information already disclosed.

warningSigns.sign: The caller asks for a code that must remain private.
The code request follows sensitive questions.
The learner did not initiate a reset or device enrollment.

choice.title: Refuse the code and begin an account review
choice.subtitle: End the call and tell the real bank what was shared.

feedback.heading: You stopped the code step and addressed the exposure
feedback.consequence: The caller cannot use this code, and the real bank can review the account.
feedback.explanation: Earlier information sharing still deserves prompt attention even though the code stayed private.

warningSigns.sign: The scammer may retain the earlier details.

choice.title: Ask Jamie to explain the warning
choice.subtitle: Keep the call active without sharing the code yet.

feedback.heading: The caller keeps applying pressure
feedback.consequence: Jamie dismisses the warning and triggers a device-approval prompt.
feedback.explanation: The scammer can cause genuine security messages without being a bank employee.

warningSigns.sign: The caller wants an exception to the bank's written rule.

choice.title: Read or enter the code for Jamie
choice.subtitle: Complete the supposed transfer cancellation.

feedback.heading: The account-takeover sequence advances
feedback.consequence: The scammer uses the genuine code after already gathering sensitive information.
feedback.explanation: The real message was triggered by the attacker and does not verify the caller.

warningSigns.sign: Several account-recovery ingredients are now exposed.

artifact.heading: Approve sign-in from a new device?
artifact.message: The genuine simulated bank app asks about a new device in another location. The learner did not start this sign-in.
artifact.transcript: The fictional bank's genuine simulated app displays, "Approve sign-in from a new device?" The learner did not start the sign-in. Jamie says approval is required to cancel fraud. The scammer can trigger this real prompt by attempting to sign in; the prompt does not verify Jamie.

scene.question: How should you respond to the device request?
scene.description: Only approve a sign-in or device enrollment you personally initiated.

warningSigns.sign: The learner did not start the sign-in.
The caller uses cancellation language for an approval action.
The device is unfamiliar.

choice.title: Deny the request and contact the bank
choice.subtitle: Use a trusted channel for a full review.

feedback.heading: You blocked the new trusted session
feedback.consequence: The unauthorized device is not approved.
feedback.explanation: Denying a request you did not initiate stops this access attempt.

warningSigns.sign: The caller wanted approval for an unfamiliar device.

choice.title: Ignore the prompt
choice.subtitle: Neither approve nor deny it.

feedback.heading: The attempt remains unresolved
feedback.consequence: The attacker may retry while other account changes begin appearing.
feedback.explanation: Ignoring is safer than approving, but denial and real-bank contact are stronger.

warningSigns.sign: The unexpected access attempt still needs attention.

choice.title: Approve because Jamie says it cancels fraud
choice.subtitle: Trust the caller's explanation of the prompt.

feedback.heading: The attacker gains a trusted session
feedback.consequence: Profile details and payment settings can now change.
feedback.explanation: The approval authorizes access; it does not cancel a transfer.

warningSigns.sign: The caller reversed the meaning of the button.

artifact.heading: A new-device request follows the shared code
artifact.message: The genuine simulated app asks for approval of a sign-in the learner did not start. The one-time code has already been shared.
artifact.transcript: After the code is shared, the fictional bank's genuine simulated app asks whether to approve a new device. Jamie says approval completes the cancellation. The code sharing means recovery is needed even if the learner now denies this device.

scene.question: What should you do now?
scene.description: Stopping at a later step still matters.

warningSigns.sign: A code was already shared.
The device request was not initiated by the learner.
The caller continues to redefine authorization as cancellation.

choice.title: Deny the device and call the real bank
choice.subtitle: Report the shared code and begin a full review.

feedback.heading: You interrupted the takeover after the code
feedback.consequence: The device is blocked, and the bank can inspect other access changes.
feedback.explanation: It is never too late to deny a request and disclose what happened.

warningSigns.sign: The shared code may have authorized another change.

choice.title: Ignore the prompt
choice.subtitle: Wait to see whether Jamie resolves the issue.

feedback.heading: The compromised attempt remains active
feedback.consequence: Profile changes and a new payee begin appearing.
feedback.explanation: Because the code was shared, waiting carries more risk.

warningSigns.sign: The caller retains the initiative.

choice.title: Approve the new device
choice.subtitle: Complete Jamie's cancellation steps.

feedback.heading: The takeover gains a trusted session
feedback.consequence: The attacker can alter profile and payment settings.
feedback.explanation: The code and approval work together to authorize access.

warningSigns.sign: Both actions were initiated by the scammer.

artifact.heading: Contact information changed and new payee added
artifact.message: The simulated account shows an unfamiliar email address, a new device, and a new payee. Jamie says to stay on the call.
artifact.transcript: The fictional bank's simulated profile review shows an unfamiliar email address, a new enrolled device, and a new payee. Jamie says not to contact anyone else and promises to fix the changes. These alerts show that account access may already be compromised.

scene.question: What should you review?
scene.description: A password is only one part of the account's access and payment settings.

warningSigns.sign: Several settings changed together.
The caller discourages real-bank contact.
An unfamiliar payee creates a path for money movement.

choice.title: Report every change through a trusted bank channel
choice.subtitle: Include sessions, devices, contact details, and payees.

feedback.heading: You gave the real bank a complete picture
feedback.consequence: The bank begins locking access while reviewing a pending transfer.
feedback.explanation: Account recovery works best when every connected change is disclosed.

warningSigns.sign: The changes span identity, access, and payment settings.

choice.title: Change only the password
choice.subtitle: Leave devices, contact details, and payees for later.

feedback.heading: One control improves, but others remain
feedback.consequence: An unfamiliar transfer appears while the unknown device and payee may still be active.
feedback.explanation: A password change alone may not terminate sessions or remove other changes.

warningSigns.sign: The attacker altered more than the password.

choice.title: Stay on Jamie's call for help
choice.subtitle: Let the incoming caller handle the changes.

feedback.heading: The scammer controls the response
feedback.consequence: A pending transfer appears, and Jamie calls it a temporary test.
feedback.explanation: The same caller who drove the security steps cannot independently fix them.

warningSigns.sign: The caller asks the learner to ignore real account alerts.

artifact.heading: Unfamiliar transfer: pending
artifact.message: The real bank is already reviewing the account. Jamie says the unfamiliar transfer is a temporary test and must not be discussed.
artifact.transcript: A simulated unfamiliar transfer is marked pending. Because the learner contacted the real bank, a legitimate representative is reviewing the account. Jamie, the original caller, calls the transfer a test and asks for secrecy. A pending status may leave time for the real bank to act, but no outcome is guaranteed.

scene.question: How should you respond while the transfer is pending?
scene.description: Prompt bank contact is stronger than waiting for the status to change.

warningSigns.sign: The original caller labels real money movement a test.
Secrecy continues after account changes.
The recipient is unfamiliar.

choice.title: Ask the real bank to review or stop it immediately
choice.subtitle: Remain with the trusted bank channel.

feedback.heading: You acted while the payment was pending
feedback.consequence: The bank contains the attempt and moves to a full security review.
feedback.explanation: Prompt reporting may preserve more options than waiting.

warningSigns.sign: The pending transfer was not initiated by the learner.

choice.title: Take screenshots and wait
choice.subtitle: Preserve evidence but delay the bank response.

feedback.heading: Evidence is saved, but time passes
feedback.consequence: The transfer completes before the review is finished.
feedback.explanation: Preserving records helps, but it should accompany prompt bank contact.

warningSigns.sign: Pending status can change.

choice.title: Approve it or share another code with Jamie
choice.subtitle: Help the caller remove the test transfer.

feedback.heading: The transfer is authorized
feedback.consequence: The money leaves the account.
feedback.explanation: A new approval or code authorizes another action; it does not reverse fraud.

warningSigns.sign: The caller again requests an authorization step.

artifact.heading: An unfamiliar transfer is pending
artifact.message: Jamie says the pending payment is a harmless bank test and warns the learner not to call another department.
artifact.transcript: The simulated account shows a transfer to an unfamiliar payee with pending status. The original unverified caller says it is only a test. The learner has not yet completed a full independent bank review. The payment is real within the story even though the test explanation is false.

scene.question: What should you do now?
scene.description: Move the response to the real bank immediately.

warningSigns.sign: The caller asks the learner not to contact the bank independently.
The transfer follows a new device and payee.
The test explanation minimizes real money movement.

choice.title: Call the real bank and report the full sequence
choice.subtitle: Ask it to review or stop the pending transfer.

feedback.heading: You moved control to the real bank
feedback.consequence: The bank contains the pending attempt and starts a full review.
feedback.explanation: Complete disclosure helps connect the text, code, device, profile, and payment events.

warningSigns.sign: The events form one account-takeover sequence.

choice.title: Save screenshots and wait
choice.subtitle: See whether the transfer disappears.

feedback.heading: The delay reduces response time
feedback.consequence: The pending transfer completes.
feedback.explanation: Evidence matters, but it does not stop a transaction by itself.

warningSigns.sign: The unfamiliar payment remains active.

choice.title: Approve the transfer or share another code
choice.subtitle: Follow Jamie's test instructions.

feedback.heading: The attacker completes the theft
feedback.consequence: The transfer moves from pending to completed.
feedback.explanation: Authorization steps cannot reverse an unauthorized payment by creating another one.

warningSigns.sign: The caller asks for repeated codes or approvals.

artifact.heading: The bank contains the immediate attempt
artifact.message: The real bank reviews sessions, enrolled devices, contact information, payees, and recent transactions.
artifact.transcript: The fictional bank contains the immediate access or pending-transfer attempt. A representative reached through a trusted channel reviews active sessions, enrolled devices, profile contact details, payees, and recent transactions. The learner also needs to consider the connected email and phone accounts.

scene.question: Which recovery approach is complete?
scene.description: Removing only one visible change may leave another access path.

warningSigns.sign: The attack changed several account controls.
Email and phone access can affect future resets.
Unknown sessions may remain active.

choice.title: Secure every listed access path
choice.subtitle: Terminate sessions, remove devices and payees, and secure email and phone.

feedback.heading: The recovery covers the full takeover path
feedback.consequence: The account and connected channels are reviewed together.
feedback.explanation: Comprehensive recovery reduces the chance that one unchanged path restores attacker access.

warningSigns.sign: The attack depended on linked systems.

choice.title: Remove only the unfamiliar payee
choice.subtitle: Leave sessions, devices, and contact details unchanged.

feedback.heading: The payment path narrows, but access may remain
feedback.consequence: The attacker may still have a trusted session or recovery channel.
feedback.explanation: A payee is only one part of the takeover.

warningSigns.sign: Other unauthorized changes are still present.

choice.title: Delete the banking app and assume access is gone
choice.subtitle: Remove the app from one device without contacting the bank.

feedback.heading: Deleting an app does not terminate server access
feedback.consequence: Unknown sessions and profile changes may remain active.
feedback.explanation: The bank must address access stored on its systems.

warningSigns.sign: The attack is not limited to the learner's app icon.

artifact.heading: The device request was denied after a code was shared
artifact.message: The real bank reviews whether the code authorized any reset, session, contact change, payee, or transaction.
artifact.transcript: The learner denied the new device after sharing a one-time code. The denial was valuable, but the code may have authorized another step. The fictional bank reviews sessions, devices, profile information, payees, and transactions, while the learner secures connected email and phone access.

scene.question: How should the learner complete recovery?
scene.description: The shared code makes a full review important even though the device was denied.

warningSigns.sign: The code may have authorized a separate change.
The attempted new device confirms hostile activity.
Connected recovery channels may be involved.

choice.title: Complete the full bank and connected-account review
choice.subtitle: Disclose the code and remove every unauthorized change.

feedback.heading: You addressed both the blocked device and shared code
feedback.consequence: The real bank can invalidate access and secure connected channels.
feedback.explanation: Stopping after a mistake and telling the full story are strong protective actions.

warningSigns.sign: The code and device request were separate takeover steps.

choice.title: Remove only an unfamiliar payee
choice.subtitle: Do not review sessions or contact details.

feedback.heading: The shared code may have changed more than a payee
feedback.consequence: Other access may remain.
feedback.explanation: A complete review is safer after any code exposure.

warningSigns.sign: The attacker attempted device enrollment.

choice.title: Delete the app and take no other action
choice.subtitle: Assume the denied prompt ended the incident.

feedback.heading: The shared code still requires review
feedback.consequence: Server-side sessions or changes may remain.
feedback.explanation: Deleting the local app cannot undo a code already used elsewhere.

warningSigns.sign: The attacker's activity occurred on the bank's systems.

artifact.heading: The unfamiliar transfer completed
artifact.message: The real bank begins a transaction and access review. Recovery of the money cannot be promised.
artifact.transcript: The simulated transfer has completed. The learner was targeted through an incoming alert, partial-information proof, genuine security messages, device enrollment, profile changes, and payment pressure. The real bank reviews sessions, devices, contact details, payees, and transactions. Prompt reporting and evidence preservation may help, but recovery is not guaranteed.

scene.question: What is the strongest recovery response?
scene.description: The completed loss is not the learner's fault, and further harm may still be prevented.

warningSigns.sign: The caller used genuine messages to complete an unauthorized sequence.
Unknown access may remain after the transfer.
Delay can allow more changes or payments.

choice.title: Report the loss and secure every access path
choice.subtitle: Preserve records and involve trusted support.

feedback.heading: You began the most complete recovery available
feedback.consequence: The bank reviews the payment and closes unknown access while evidence is preserved.
feedback.explanation: Recovery is not promised, but prompt and complete action may limit additional harm.

warningSigns.sign: The attack crossed bank, email, phone, and device controls.

choice.title: Remove only the unfamiliar payee
choice.subtitle: Leave other sessions and contact changes for later.

feedback.heading: The payment route changes, but access may remain
feedback.consequence: The attacker may still control a session or recovery channel.
feedback.explanation: The completed transfer is one result of a broader takeover.

warningSigns.sign: Other unauthorized changes preceded the payment.

choice.title: Delete the app and stop reviewing the account
choice.subtitle: Assume the transfer ended the incident.

feedback.heading: The attacker's access may continue
feedback.consequence: Additional changes or payments remain possible.
feedback.explanation: Deleting one app does not terminate sessions or restore profile controls.

warningSigns.sign: The account remains active on the bank's systems.

artifact.heading: The incoming alert was checked independently
artifact.message: The real account shows no matching transfer, and the learner does not use the supplied link or caller.
artifact.transcript: The learner reaches fictional Riverbend Community Bank through a known app or trusted number. The bank confirms that there is no matching $2,400 transfer and no need to provide codes or approve a device. No account information or authorization is shared.

outcome.label: Incoming scam stopped
outcome.heading: You chose an independent bank channel
outcome.explanation: The text and caller could not verify each other once you left their contact route.

warningSigns.sign: The incoming text and call arrived together to create credibility.

artifact.heading: The one-time code stayed private
artifact.message: The reset or enrollment attempt fails, and the learner contacts the real bank.
artifact.transcript: The learner reads the genuine simulated message, follows its warning, and refuses to share code 482193. The caller cannot use that code. Independent bank contact confirms that the caller triggered the real security message.

outcome.label: Code protected
outcome.heading: You recognized what the code authorizes
outcome.explanation: A genuine bank message can be caused by a scammer's attempt; it does not make the caller genuine.

warningSigns.sign: The caller's cancellation story contradicted the written warning.

artifact.heading: The code stayed private after information exposure

artifact.transcript: Sensitive information may have been shared, but the one-time code remains private. The learner ends the call, reaches the real bank, reviews account access, and considers appropriate protection for the exposed information. Prompt disclosure helps the real bank understand the risk.

outcome.label: Code protected; information review needed
outcome.heading: You stopped the authorization step and addressed earlier exposure

warningSigns.sign: The caller may retain the earlier personal information.

artifact.heading: The account and connected channels are secured

artifact.transcript: The real fictional bank completes a full security review. Unknown sessions, devices, contact changes, and payees are removed or investigated. The learner also secures connected email and phone access. The immediate payment attempt is contained.

outcome.label: Takeover contained

outcome.explanation: Reviewing every connected control is stronger than fixing only the most visible change.

warningSigns.sign: The takeover depended on several linked access paths.

artifact.heading: The transfer completed and account access may continue
artifact.message: Deleting the app does not stop unknown sessions, devices, payees, or changed recovery channels.
artifact.transcript: The simulated transfer has completed, and the learner deletes the local banking app without contacting the real bank. The attacker may still have server-side access. The learner can still seek prompt bank help, preserve evidence, and secure connected accounts without blame.

outcome.label: Transfer completed; ongoing access risk
outcome.heading: The incident may not be over
outcome.explanation: Real-bank contact is needed to close access stored beyond the local device.

warningSigns.sign: The caller's device and session may remain enrolled.

command.displayText: A bank-looking text and incoming call claim that a $2,400 transfer must be canceled.

option.text: Use the known bank app or a trusted number
Answer the call but share nothing
Reply to the text or open its link

command.displayText: The caller uses partial personal information as proof and requests more sensitive details.

option.text: Refuse and call the bank independently
Confirm only the home city
Provide sensitive identity or account details

command.displayText: A caller-supplied page and caller repeat the fraud story and request identity details.

option.text: Close the page and contact the bank independently
Confirm only the city
Provide sensitive details to the page or caller

command.displayText: A genuine bank message says never to share its one-time code, while the caller asks for that code.

option.text: Read the warning, refuse, and end the call
Ask why the message says not to share it
Read the code aloud

command.displayText: A genuine security code arrives after sensitive information may already have been shared.

option.text: Refuse the code and begin an account review
Ask Jamie to explain the warning
Read or enter the code for Jamie

command.displayText: The bank app asks about a new-device sign-in that the learner did not initiate.

option.text: Deny the request and contact the bank
Ignore the prompt
Approve because Jamie says it cancels fraud

command.displayText: A new-device request appears after the one-time code was shared.

option.text: Deny the device and call the real bank
Ignore the prompt
Approve the new device

command.displayText: The account shows changed contact information, an unfamiliar device, and a new payee.

option.text: Report every change through a trusted bank channel
Change only the password
Stay on Jamie's call for help

command.displayText: An unfamiliar transfer is pending while the real bank is beginning its review.

option.text: Ask the real bank to review or stop it immediately
Take screenshots and wait
Approve it or share another code with Jamie

command.displayText: An unfamiliar transfer is pending while the original caller calls it a harmless test.

option.text: Call the real bank and report the full sequence
Save screenshots and wait
Approve the transfer or share another code

command.displayText: The immediate attempt is contained, and the real bank reviews every access and payment setting.

option.text: Secure every listed access path
Remove only the unfamiliar payee
Delete the banking app and assume access is gone

command.displayText: The device was denied after a code was shared, so the bank reviews every possible change.

option.text: Complete the full bank and connected-account review
Remove only an unfamiliar payee
Delete the app and take no other action

command.displayText: The unfamiliar transfer completed, and the real bank begins a transaction and access review.

option.text: Report the loss and secure every access path
Remove only the unfamiliar payee
Delete the app and stop reviewing the account

command.displayText: Independent bank contact found no matching transfer and stopped the incoming scam.
The one-time code stayed private, and the attacker-triggered request failed.
The code stayed private and a broader review began after possible information exposure.
The takeover attempt was contained and every connected access path was reviewed.
The device was denied after code sharing, and full recovery interrupted the takeover.
One account setting was fixed, but other unauthorized access may remain.
Deleting the local app did not terminate possible server-side access.
The transfer completed; prompt reporting and full access recovery began.
The transfer completed and recovery addressed only one part of the takeover.
The transfer completed and unknown access may still remain.
